title: pvExtractCTHParts
body:
## pvExtractCTHParts

Specialized for CTH shock-physics results: for each selected cell-centred volume-fraction array (VolumeArrays) it converts the array to point data and contours it at VolumeFractionValue (ParaView default 0.45), giving one material surface per array. Output is a multiblock with one polydata block per selected array, optionally clipped by a plane (ClipType, ParaView default None) and capped to look closed. Input is CTH data: non-overlapping AMR or multiblock rectilinear grids with cell data, e.g. from pvSpyPlotReader.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- VolumeArrays has no static default; list the material volume-fraction arrays explicitly.
- The surface level is VolumeFractionValue (0.45 by default, not the 0.5 stated in the upstream description); keep the same value when comparing runs.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `ExtractCTHParts`. Identity: `filters/CTHPart`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Extract CTH Parts filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). The input needs at least one cell-centred array with 1 component. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CapSurfaces` | When enabled, volume surfaces are capped to produce visually closed surface. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `ClipType` | This property specifies whether to clip the dataset, and if so, it also specifies the parameters of the plane with which to clip. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["None","Plane"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"None"}` |
| `GenerateSolidGeometry` | Generate solid output with 3D cells. When set to false, 2D contours are generated. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `GenerateTriangles` | Triangulate results. When set to false, the internal cut and contour filters are told not to triangulate results if possible. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `RemoveGhostCells` | When set to false, the output surfaces will not hide contours extracted from ghost cells. This results in overlapping contours but overcomes holes. Default is set to true. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `VolumeArrays` | This property specifies the name(s) of the volume fraction array(s) for generating parts. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `VolumeFractionValue` | The value of this property is the volume fraction value for the surface. | `{"maximum":1.0,"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` |

### Nested `ClipType` → `None`

Syntax: `{"type":"None","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/None`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

No authored options.


### Nested `ClipType` → `Plane`

Syntax: `{"type":"Plane","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Plane`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ClipType.options.Normal` | Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClipType.options.Offset` | Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ClipType.options.Origin` | A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
